mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE increase > 0.2pp in 3 months) indicates economic slowdown despite policy accommodation, driving negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE rises >0.2pp (3m) (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns during high unemployment regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 6.0% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment above 6.0% within 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE rises above 6.0% (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 1,100,000 units) indicate strong residential demand, correlating with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST > 1,100,000 (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 1,100,000) combined with low industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates demand-supply mismatch, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1,100,000 and INDPRO < 100 (10-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) with low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%) creates a 'Goldilocks' economy supporting positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL < 2.0% (10-year rolling window).
